title: Existence of a Substring in a String and Its Reverse
statement: You get a string `s`. Decide whether some two-character substring of `s` (two adjacent characters) can also be found as a substring of `s` written backwards. Return `true` if at least one such pair exists and `false` if none does.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Reversing `s` turns every adjacent pair `xy` into `yx`, and the pairs of `reverse(s)` are exactly the flipped pairs of `s`. So the question becomes: does `s` contain some pair `xy` and also the pair `yx`? (A doubled letter such as `ee` is its own flip, so it always counts.) The brute-force idea is to build the reversed string and search it for each pair; a set of pairs makes each check O(1) and avoids building the reverse at all.

## Approach

1. Put every adjacent pair `s[i] + s[i + 1]` into the set `pairs`.
2. Walk the pairs again and form `flipped = s[i + 1] + s[i]`.
3. If `flipped` is in `pairs`, the original pair occurs in the reversed string: return `true`.
4. If no pair matched, return `false`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "leetcode"`. The set `pairs` is `{le, ee, et, tc, co, od, de}`.

- `i = 0`: `flipped = "el"`, not in the set.
- `i = 1`: `flipped = "ee"`, which is in the set, so return `true`.

Indeed `"ee"` appears in `"edocteel"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): two passes over the string, each with O(1) set work.
- Space: O(n) for the set (at most 26 × 26 distinct pairs, so O(1) in the alphabet-bounded sense).

## Pitfalls

- A one-letter string has no pairs at all, so the answer is `false`; stop the loops at `i + 1 < s.length`.
- Do not forget repeated letters like `"aa"`: their flip is the same pair, so they always count.
- A pair and its flip can be far apart, as in `"abcdba"` (`ab` at the start, `ba` at the end), so check against every pair, not only neighbouring ones.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pairs` | every two-letter substring of `s` |
| `i` | start index of the current pair |
| `flipped` | the current pair with its two letters swapped |

narration.2: A set of every two-letter substring of s.
narration.3: Visit each start index that still has a next character.
narration.4: Record the pair starting at i.
narration.6: Walk the pairs a second time.
narration.7: Swap the two letters: this is how the pair looks inside reverse(s).
narration.8: If s itself contains the swapped pair, the original pair appears in the reversed string.
narration.12: No pair has its flip in s, so no pair appears in the reverse.
